hook_text: One town powered South Africa for fifty years. Here is the bill it never showed you.
clip_script: A coal town on the Highveld: miners underground, a power station lighting the whole country, busy shops on payday. That is development. Now look up: grey winter smoke, kids coughing. Look down: orange acid water seeping from an old mine into the stream. That is the environment paying. Now the mine closes. A man who drilled coal for twenty years is able, willing and looking for work, but nothing fits his skills. That is structural unemployment. In South Africa about one in three people in the labour force cannot find work. So do we keep burning coal? No. Do we abandon the town? Also no. Build solar and wind right there, retrain the workers, clean the land. That is a just transition, and it is what sustainable development looks like.
visual_style: A whiteboard town with a smokestack and a mine shaft, grey clouds and an orange stream drawn in, then the smokestack crossed out and wind turbines and solar panels drawn beside a retrained worker.
mood: Serious and honest, turning into practical hope.
pacing: A proud opening, a slow reveal of the costs, a brisk solution at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out how to grow without wrecking tomorrow.
